messages:
Maya: Heads-up — customer ACME hitting /v1/embeddings with large batched requests (~120 rps). They see intermittent wrong-length vectors: some responses are length 1536 but their pipeline expects 1024. Getting 400 + occasional partial success.
SupportBot: Created ticket INC-7882 and linked to the customer record. :eyes:
Sam: Which SDK(s) are they using? TS, Python, Go? Any sample request/resp?
Maya: They use ts-sdk in frontend aggregator and go client in a background worker. Error payload from API: `{"error":"embedding_dim_mismatch","expected":1024,"got":1536}`. Logs attached in ticket (sensitive bits redacted).
Olivia: That error usually means mixed-model batching or wrong model param passed. Can you paste the request body (sanitized) or a minimal repro?
Maya: TS client snippet from their aggregator:```js
// ts-sdk snippet (sanitized)
await client.embeddings.create({
  model: 'embed-1024',
  input: batchOfTexts // array of 40 items
})
```
And their router sometimes merges items from another service that calls `embed-1536`. Go worker snippet:```go
// go client
resp, err := client.Embeddings(ctx, &EmbeddingsRequest{Model: "embed-1024", Input: docs})
```
Tom: Hmm — looks like upstream router is mixing items from two services into one POST (one uses embed-1024, other embed-1536) then sets model param to 1024. API should validate per-item model if items can vary, but we don't accept mixed-dimension batches.
Diego: I tried to repro locally by batching mixed models into a single request. Repro steps: 1) send POST with input length 40 where first 20 were encoded by embed-1536 pipeline and rest by embed-1024. 2) Server returns 400 with the json error above. But interestingly in a few runs the runtime streamed back vectors of len 1536 for some items (and still returned header expected=1024) — suggests a race in kernel selection for fused batches.
Sam: That streaming-of-wrong-length is concerning. Assign to eng-ml to investigate kernel selection + batch routing. @Diego can you open an internal bug with the repro, logs, and latency/throughput profiles? Include the exact request bodies (sanitized) and the response bodies.
Diego: Doing that now. Also capturing traces — I see the batcher accepting items before model validation completes if the batcher merges queues. Suspect path: batcher groups by shard only, not by model variant.
Maya: Customer wants mitigation steps ASAP. Workarounds we recommended: (1) Ensure upstream router does per-model grouping or call embeddings per-model; (2) Temporarily reduce batch sizes so cross-service merges are less likely; (3) If using SDKs, add client-side validation to check model param per request and fail fast if mismatched.
Olivia: For SDKs: we should add a defensive check when the `input` is an array of objects that include a `model` field or metadata. Also add a guardrail that asserts returned vector length equals model-profiled dim and surface a clear error before streaming.
Tom: I'll prepare a small patch to TS and Go SDKs to validate dims against known model catalogue at call time (local map of model->dim) and fail fast. Will add retry jitter improvements on the client side to avoid amplifying bursts. :shipit:
Sam: Also add server-side hard validation in the router: refuse to merge requests where the effective model differs; respond 400 with helpful hint. That should be quick to push as a feature-flagged change.
Maya: Customer notified of the temporary mitigations and will try per-model calls this afternoon. They're asking for ETA to permanent fix.
Diego: Internal bug INC-7882-ENG created with repro, traces, and failing test. Assigned to eng-ml. ETA request pending — will try to get a debug/tracing patch within 24h and a full fix timeline after root cause confirmed.
SupportBot: Ticket INC-7882 updated: status -> triaged, assignee -> eng-ml (Diego).
Tom: Quick note — observed differences in retry/timeouts between SDKs: TS default deadline=10s, Go=30s — explain why Go sometimes EOFs (deadline exceeded on connection) while TS bubbles the 400 quicker. We'll normalize defaults and document recommended settings for high-throughput batching.
Maya: Thanks all. Please keep updates in the ticket and drop short notes here if you hit anything new. :thumbsup:
